rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (line_loss search_right) returned metrics identical to iteration 4 (last_direction) to four decimal places on all three tracks: score 53.7076, max_error 0.0607, 0.0648 and 0.0621, one line-loss event per trial, and 0 completions. Recovery direction therefore has no measurable effect, and the excursion that pushes the robot past the 0.06 m off-track limit happens before or independently of the recovery steering. The results so far are: ki 0.4 changed nothing (bias hypothesis not supported); kd 0.15 gave a tiny gain (+0.9) with no change in max_error; widening the sensors to +/-0.05 cut progress (controller signal averaging weakens steering); and every design, including the 1.6 base_speed baseline, still shows max_error of about 0.060 to 0.065 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and even body_width 0.18 gives only 0.0575, so the limit cannot be raised with geometry. The line is lost at about 0.05 m offset (16 mm sensors at +/-0.03 see the tape out to about 0.0505 m), so the robot is already drifting off the line before the loss.

Change. Following the Evaluator's rule for an unchanged result, I revert controller.line_loss to last_direction, since it is physically sensible and search_right gave no benefit. I also test base_speed 1.25 (down from 1.4), the one untested variable that acts on bend entry. Geometry (x = +/-0.03 with 16 mm footprints, y = 0.03), kp 1.5, ki 0 and kd 0.15 are unchanged, so any change is attributable to speed. The 1.6 baseline did not cure the excursion, but it was run with kp 2.0 and kd 0.05 and a 12 mm footprint, so speed was never isolated.

Expected result. If bend-entry speed drives the drift, max_error should fall below about 0.060 m, line_loss_events should drop on some seeds, and progress should rise past the current 0.12 to 0.16. Completion is still unlikely at 1.25 (about 3.5 s or more for the course), so completion_time will be the limit once the line is held. If max_error is still about 0.06 to 0.065 m with one loss per trial, speed is not the limit either, and the next test should be kp (e.g. 2.0 with kd 0.15) to check whether stiffer steering corrects the drift before the 0.05 m loss.

Hypotheses to check. (1) Lower speed reduces the drift at bends, so max_error falls and progress rises. (2) The excursion comes from a fixed transient at the start or first bend, and speed has no effect. (3) Progress gain from a longer run is worth more to the score (250 x progress) than the time term, so a slower but longer run should help while the robot stays on the line.
